task: Phase E Track B, B2 part c: do EXISTING SYSTEMS (LLM observability, agent eval harnesses, Claude Code/Codex logging, capture-side systems of CLAUDE_context_swarms.md §5) record provider request ids AND use them to verify, order or bound anything?
scope_note: Systems only. The literature on request-id structure and trusted timestamping belongs to B2a/B2b (sibling files). Everything here comes from reading source at pinned commits or vendor docs, plus the six §5 papers via alphaXiv. Nothing related to the local Qwen swarm was read. No transcripts were generated. No paid API calls. Dead ends (§7) not cited.
question: Does any existing system record provider request ids and use them to verify, order or bound anything?

answer.bottom_line: No. Of 25 systems examined in 23 table rows (19 open or documented products, harnesses and standards, one row covering SWE-bench, SWE-agent and mini-swe-agent, plus 6 capture-side papers, with code where released), none uses a provider-minted request id, or any other provider-side clock, to verify, order or bound anything. Recording is common; using it for time is absent.

counts.record_provider_transport_request_id: 6 (Langfuse ai-gateway; W&B Weave for the OpenAI SDK; Codex, only in opt-in rollout-trace, feedback tags and auth OTel events; Claude Code transcript and OTel; LiteLLM, exposed as llm_provider-* headers with persistence unverified; Vivaria, semantics undocumented, counted as unclear). Read-only consumers of Claude Code's requestId: ccusage, Braintrust bt-daemon, Harbor's Claude Code adapter.
counts.record_provider_response_or_message_id_o: LangSmith, OpenLLMetry, OTel GenAI semconv, Inspect (raw body), mini-swe-agent (raw body + `created`), OpenHands SDK, Tracekit, NovaFabric; Helicone keeps the provider body only (not verified field-level)
counts.use_provider_id_for_correlation_or_suppo: Claude Code OTel ('message-level reconstruction'), Codex feedback tags, Langfuse metadata, Braintrust errors.py (its own API)
counts.use_provider_id_for_dedupe_or_grouping: ccusage, Harbor (Devin dedupe, Claude Code bundling), Braintrust bt-daemon, OpenHands batch atomicity, Tracekit, LiteLLM SpendLogs PK

nearest_things: Langfuse ai-gateway and Codex rollout-trace each store the provider request id next to their own wall clock in one record. They hold the bracket's ingredients but never relate them.

ccusage recognises a response copied into several Claude Code session transcripts by (message.id, requestId), the same resume/fork phenomenon as FINDINGS ids/O7. It deduplicates and does not compare times.
NovaFabric orders events by self-minted ULIDs and explicitly disclaims that this is independent of the emitter's clock: exactly the property a provider-minted id would add.
Hearsay names 'the model provider's own request log' as the next witness out and does not build it. Its own ledger timestamps are explicitly not bound as evidence.

Adjacent, not request ids: Anthropic's API internally verifies that the conversation prefix (system, tools, all prior messages including tool_results) is unchanged before it accepts a replayed thinking block (new accounts from 2026-08-31; Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5). It is server-side only, needs paid calls, and catches post-hoc edits, not execution-path fabrication.

claims.claim: B2 headline, systems view: an existing system already decodes the time in a provider-minted request id and uses it as a clock the agent does not control, to bound, order or verify agent tool-log timestamps (the skew bracket: id time between the stream's last input and the response's first output).
claims.closest_work: Mechanically: Langfuse ai-gateway (langfuse/langfuse@f75c661d) and Codex rollout-trace (openai/codex@ab452649), which co-record the provider request id with their own wall clock. Conceptually: Hearsay (arXiv 2609.32495) App. I, which names the provider's request log as the next witness.
claims.what_it_does: Langfuse records `langfuse.gateway.upstream.request.id` next to start_time_unix_ms / first_byte_ms. Codex records `upstream_request_id` next to wall_time_unix_ms and a contiguous seq. Claude Code persists `requestId` beside each assistant row's timestamp. Hearsay argues the provider's own request log is 'the one witness the operator does not run'.
claims.what_it_does_not: None of the 25 systems examined decodes the request id, treats it as a clock, compares it with the harness/gateway clock, or uses it to order or bound anything. Hearsay does not implement its pointer, and its witness is an instrumented proxy, not an id already in the native record.
claims.deciding_citation: langfuse/langfuse ai-gateway/src/telemetry/mapping.rs L183-189 (`("upstream.request.id", &facts.inference.provider_request_id)` inserted as metadata, no other consumer besides observability/metrics.rs L96-99); openai/codex codex-rs/rollout-trace/src/reducer/inference.rs L211-217 (stored only); Hearsay p.48 'The next writer out is the model provider's own request log, the one witness the operator does not run.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: verdict scoped to SYSTEMS (B2 part c), not the literature (B2a/B2b). Every listed system was checked in source or docs at a pinned commit. Uses found are correlation, support lookup, dedupe and grouping. Zero uses for time, ordering or bounding. Residual risk: closed-source back ends (LangSmith server, Braintrust server, Helicone hosted, Claude Code core, METR Middleman, Anthropic's own systems) could do something internally; that cannot be checked from outside.

claims.claim: Precondition: provider request ids already sit in records that exist without instrumenting the agent, so the mechanism can run on past logs.
claims.closest_work: Claude Code transcripts and OTel (docs); Codex rollout-trace; Langfuse gateway; Weave; LiteLLM headers
claims.what_it_does: Present by default: Claude Code JSONL (`requestId` on assistant rows) and Claude Code OTel `request_id` (when telemetry is enabled). Present when a specific component is in the path: Langfuse ai-gateway (not the SDK); W&B Weave for OpenAI SDK calls; LiteLLM `_hidden_params` additional_headers as `llm_provider-request-id` (persistence not verified); Codex only in opt-in rollout-trace bundles (CODEX_ROLLOUT_TRACE_ROOT) and feedback tags; Vivaria `request_id` with undocumented semantics.
claims.what_it_does_not: Not recorded: Inspect (mints its own x-irid), Helicone (own UUIDs), LangSmith SDK, OpenLLMetry and OTel GenAI (response id only), OpenInference, SWE-bench, SWE-agent, mini-swe-agent (response id and `created` only), OpenHands SDK (response id only), Harbor ATIF (only via `extra`, for Devin/Cursor/Claude Code adapters), Tracekit (drops requestId), AFR, NovaFabric (response id only), ACE, Hearsay, Tool Receipts.
claims.deciding_citation: code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage: '`request_id` on the API events, persisted as `requestId` on the transcript's assistant entries'; openai/codex rollout-trace/src/raw_event.rs L105-108; Inspect hooks.py L70 `REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "x-irid"`.
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: a factual coverage item, not a novelty claim, so N/A. It bounds the B4 request-id column: by default only Claude Code writes the provider request id into its native transcript. Every other source needs a specific gateway or SDK, or opt-in diagnostics.

claims.claim: Using provider-minted ids (request id / message id / response id) as join, dedupe or grouping keys over agent logs, including recognising one response copied into several session transcripts (our resume/fork copy handling, FINDINGS ids/O7).
claims.what_it_does: Deduplicates Claude Code usage across sessions by (message.id, requestId) 'because Claude Code can copy one response into multiple session transcripts'. It also handles sidechain replays that keep the message id under a new request id. Similar grouping use: Harbor (devin.py seen_request_ids; claude_code.py one ATIF step per message.id), Braintrust bt-daemon (segment and merge by message.id/requestId), OpenHands (batch atomicity by llm_response_id), Tracekit (group model turns by message id), LiteLLM (SpendLogs primary key = response id).
claims.what_it_does_not: None of them reads time out of the id. None checks that the copy's client timestamp agrees with the original or with the id's embedded time, so none detects re-stamping or back-dating.
claims.deciding_citation: ccusage rust/adapters/claude/src/README.md: 'When `requestId` is present, both loaders deduplicate matching message and request IDs across sessions because Claude Code can copy one response into multiple session transcripts.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: recognising resume/fork copies by request id is existing practice; cite ccusage rather than present copy dedupe as ours. The remaining delta is the time comparison.

claims.claim: Ordering an agent's event log by time-ordered identifiers (UUIDv7/ULID) instead of a separate timestamp field.
claims.closest_work: NovaFabric (arXiv 2609.12582; MSKazemi/novafabric@7cc03a6a); Agent Flight Recorder (arXiv 2609.01931; mpi-dsg/agent-flight-recorder@28ddcde9)
claims.what_it_does: NovaFabric mints ULIDs (optionally UUIDv7) so an emitter's events sort by id. AFR mints 'UUIDv7-style' event ids (48-bit ms prefix from time.time()) and checks a monotonic logical_clock.
claims.what_it_does_not: Both mint ids from their OWN clock, and NovaFabric explicitly disclaims independence. Neither uses a third party's ids. Neither infers cross-emitter order from ids ('Ordering across emitters is not inferred from identifiers at all'). Neither bounds one clock with another.
claims.deciding_citation: NovaFabric §3.4: 'a ULID's leading field is a Unix millisecond reading from the emitting node's own clock, so this is a convenience of representation, not independence from that clock ... Ordering across emitters is not inferred from identifiers at all.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: reading time out of ids is known practice. What our mechanism adds is a minter (the provider) independent of the party being checked, and NovaFabric's own disclaimer states exactly that missing property. PARTIAL, not TAKEN.

claims.claim: Treating the model provider as an independent witness the operator/harness does not control, and reconciling it against the harness's record.
claims.what_it_does: Adds an environment-side second writer (logging proxy on all model traffic plus process and file capture) to an append-only, hash-chained ledger with an RFC 3161 head timestamp. A query and a reverse check reconcile it with the harness record: 28/28 write-time omissions and fabrications, and 98/115 edited copies, reported. Names the provider's request log as 'the one witness the operator does not run'.
claims.what_it_does_not: Requires instrumentation, so it cannot run on past logs. Its witness is operator-run, not provider-run. Its ledger timestamps are explicitly not evidence ('binds ... but not the timestamp'). It never uses provider-minted ids or provider clocks.
claims.deciding_citation: Hearsay App. I p.48: 'Our second writer stops at the operator's boundary (§7). The next writer out is the model provider's own request log, the one witness the operator does not run.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: the idea of a provider-side witness is stated in prior art as a direction, so it should not be claimed as a new paradigm. Using provider-minted ids already in the native record as that witness, with no access to the provider's log and no instrumentation, is not implemented anywhere examined. PARTIAL.

claims.claim: Any existing eval harness or observability product checks harness or tool timestamps against ANY provider-side clock (request-id time, OpenAI `created`, Google server-timing, HTTP Date, openai-processing-ms).
claims.closest_work: Langfuse ai-gateway (retains `openai-processing-ms` and `x-request-id` in its upstream response-header allowlist, transport/mod.rs L99-100); mini-swe-agent (persists the provider `created` next to a client timestamp)
claims.what_it_does: Time handling found: own-clock latency (Helicone, Langfuse, Inspect with time.monotonic), ISO-format validation (Harbor step.py), staleness against the verifier's own clock (NabaOS receipt.rs MAX_RECEIPT_AGE_MS), anchor-timestamp presence only (AFR), RFC 3161 on a ledger head that 'fixes only that an increment existed' (Hearsay).
claims.what_it_does_not: None compares a provider-side clock with a harness or tool timestamp.
claims.deciding_citation: harbor src/harbor/models/trajectories/step.py L93-102 (timestamp validator is format-only); afr/verifier.py (`if timestamp == 0: missing.append(...)`, the anchor time is never compared); Hearsay App. G 'The row hash binds writer, sequence, kind, reference and body, but not the timestamp.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: a negative result over the 25 systems examined, scoped like C1 (the same closed-source caveat applies).

claims.claim: No existing system verifies an agent transcript against state held by the model provider (adjacent finding, surfaced by the 'does it internally embody it' rule).
claims.closest_work: Anthropic Claude API thinking-block prefix binding ('Preserved thinking: prefix check')
claims.what_it_does: On Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, a replayed thinking block 'stays valid only while everything you sent before it is unchanged': the top-level system prompt, the tool set, and every message before the block (so earlier tool_result content is included). A changed prefix is rejected with 400 'The block is bound to a different conversation.' Enforced by default for accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 00:00 UTC; for older accounts only when `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` is set (beta header thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01). Claude Code transcripts keep the thinking signatures (Tracekit E4: thinking blocks persisted with 'only a signature').
claims.what_it_does_not: The signature is opaque and only the API verifies it, so no offline or third-party check exists. Checking needs a paid API call, and for Sonnet 5.5 the producing (or a linked) account. It covers only the prefix BEFORE each thinking block. It cannot catch execution-path fabrication, because a fake tool result was part of the prefix the model saw and is therefore 'valid'. It catches post-hoc editing of a stored transcript, not lying at write time.
claims.deciding_citation: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking: 'a thinking block stays valid only while everything you sent before it is unchanged on later requests. The checked prefix has three parts: The top-level system prompt; The set of tools; Every message before the block'. platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors: 'Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation.'
claims.verdict_reasoning: VERDICT REASONING: the provider internally verifies history integrity for its own purpose (thinking replay), which is a provider-held witness over records that already exist. It is not exposed as an audit tool, it costs API calls, and it targets a different threat (post-hoc edits) from ours (execution-path compromise). PARTIAL. Using it would break the no-paid-API constraint, so it is a morning human decision, not a build item.

limitations_for_design.point: By default only Claude Code writes the provider request id into its native transcript. Every other harness needs a specific gateway or SDK, or opt-in diagnostics (Codex rollout-trace). The mechanism's coverage is the Claude Code family plus whatever B4/B5 find; say so in the headline.
Cite ccusage for recognising resume/fork copies by request id. Our delta is the time comparison (copy re-stamped vs id time), not the dedupe.

Use NovaFabric's own disclaimer to frame the contribution: self-minted time-ordered ids are a representation convenience; a provider-minted id is a clock the recording party does not control. Unsigned ids remain re-mintable by a forger who learns the layout (FINDINGS §4.3 rank 1 blind spots).

Related work must say Hearsay proposed the provider as the next witness. Our claim is the narrow, implemented version: provider-minted ids already in the native record, no instrumentation, no access to the provider's log.

Possible second provider-held witness (thinking-signature prefix binding) against post-hoc transcript edits. It needs paid API calls, the same or a linked account, and models from mid-2026 on. Morning human decision; not buildable under the no-paid-API rule.

For B3 (harness dual rendering): Codex keeps model-visible conversation and runtime tool payloads as separate objects and says 'runtime payloads are evidence, not proof that the model saw the same bytes'. Check whether its reducer compares them before claiming novelty for a dual-rendering recount.
